title: Chapter 45

"You were awake the entire time?" Jakyeong muttered, his tone dripping with annoyance.

Il-hyun cracked one dark eye open, looking up at him. "I thought you might sneak in a kiss while I was asleep."

Jakyeong scoffed at the sheer absurdity. When he demanded to be let upstairs, Il-hyun simply ignored the request; when Jakyeong insisted on leaving alone, the man refused to unlock the elevator.

Resigned to finishing the movie, Jakyeong walked over to the mini-fridge in search of a cold drink. He grabbed a can of beer, paused, and pulled out a second for his captor.

"Thank you," Il-hyun murmured as the cold aluminum touched his palm.

Sitting side by side on the plush cushions, they drank in silence. Before long, Il-hyun tilted his head sideways, letting it come to rest against Jakyeong's shoulder. Jakyeong gave a sharp roll of his shoulder, shaking the weight off. Il-hyun leaned right back. Jakyeong shoved him off again. When the man stubbornly persisted a third time, Jakyeong gave up and let the head rest.

On screen, an overwrought melodrama about family reconciliation was playing out. Having grown up without a family of his own, Jakyeong felt zero emotional resonance—the story was aggressively dull.

He glanced sideways to find Il-hyun watching the screen with the exact same blank, unfeeling mask. When the father on screen wrapped his dying son in a tearful embrace, wailing hysterically, the display felt utterly foreign.

"If a child is diagnosed with a terminal illness... does it really make a parent weep like that?" Il-hyun asked quietly.

Jakyeong gave a slight shrug. "I don't have children. I wouldn't know."

"Surely you had parents."

Jakyeong didn't answer, taking a long pull from his can instead. He could feel Il-hyun’s heavy, dissecting gaze burning into the side of his face.

"Do you have no parents, Ja-kyeong?"

Draining the last drop of beer, a warm, hazy buzz settled over Jakyeong's nerves. When Il-hyun repeated the question, Jakyeong simply gave a slow nod. Why bother lying at this stage?

Il-hyun let out a low sound—somewhere between a sigh and a hum of comprehension. "And siblings?"

"None."

Il-hyun crushed the empty can in his fist, tossed it across the floor, and retrieved two fresh cans from the fridge. He popped the tab on one and handed it over. Jakyeong took it and drank.

"What does it feel like... to have no parents?"

Jakyeong swallowed the cold liquid, turning the question over in his mind for a quiet beat. "It feels... nice."

Il-hyun gave several slow, emphatic nods. "Naturally. I thought as much."

It was the unvarnished truth. Considering the monsters who had brought him into this world, growing up an orphan was an undeniable mercy.

Il-hyun raised his can, tapping the rim against Jakyeong's. "A toast. To the one who has no parents... and the one who will soon be rid of his. Cheers."

They tapped the aluminum together and drank. Two cans was usually Jakyeong's limit, but Il-hyun kept retrieving fresh rounds from the cellar. With every empty can rolling across the floor, the rigid tactical tension between them eroded, replaced by a loose, languid warmth.

Did he date often? When was his last serious relationship? Eventually, the man began prying into his per-contract rates, prompting Jakyeong to keep his answers evasive.

"I'm merely curious," Il-hyun coaxed. "Tell me."

"Why do you care so much? Looking to quit the corporate empire and switch careers?"

"Why not? I imagine I'd excel at it."

Jakyeong couldn't dispute that. In truth, Kang Il-hyun would likely surpass most veterans in the field. Devoid of empathy and unburdened by guilt, the profession fit the man like a bespoke suit. Picturing him posted up in the shadows, calmly leveling a sniper rifle and squeezing the trigger... the image was undeniably fitting.

And, Jakyeong admitted privately, remarkably alluring.
